solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vital statistics of calorie-consuming, generously proportioned bodies on beach

indicators.note: in an across clue, X on Y puts X after Y, so the bodies come after the beach
consuming means swallowing up, so the calorie's letter goes inside the word for plump

parts.note: generously proportioned is a polite way of saying fat
C is the standard abbreviation for calorie
a beach is made of sand
bodies or physiques are figures

explanation.surface: Someone eyeing up the measurements of well-fed sunbathers sprawled across the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vital statistics' suggests body measurements, matching the surface, but the answer is data in general. In an across clue 'on' puts the bodies after the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean hard numerical data or key details, the statistics of a matter.

clue.text: Vendetta fading, origins of enmity and odium lost in obfuscation

indicators.note: lost tells us the named starting letters drop out of the phrase

parts.note: a vendetta is a feud
fading means going, as in going or dwindling away

indicators.note: origins of picks the first letters of the words enmity and odium

explanation.surface: A long-running grudge petering out as the hostility and hatred disappear into vagueness.
explanation.walkthrough: FEUD GOING loses E (enmity) and O (odium), signalled by 'lost', leaving FUD GING.
explanation.definitionFit: Fudging an issue is blurring or evading it, which is a form of deliberate obscuring.

clue.text: Sport piece of clothing like lycra, back to front

indicators.note: piece of takes just one bit, the opening letter, of the word clothing
back to front means the final letter is shifted to the start

parts.note: lycra garments are tight-fitting, or clingy

explanation.surface: A sport whose kit is figure-hugging lycra, worn the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: C from clothing, then CLINGY with its back letter Y moved 'to front' gives YCLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Cycling is a competitive sport, raced on road and track.

clue.text: One's scared doom flows from its collapse?

definitions.text: One's scared doom flows from its collapse?

indicators.note: a collapse sends the letters of the three words tumbling into a new order

explanation.surface: Something whose fall would bring terror and death to whoever sits beneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: Damocles sat under a sword hung by a single hair, so its fall would bring doom to a frightened man.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary blade suspended over Damocles stands for an ever-present threat of disaster.

clue.text: Where stories are written — rolling Bronte country perhaps underpins novel

indicators.note: underpins puts the novel piece beneath, so in this down entry it comes after the other

parts.note: novel as an adjective means new

indicators.note: rolling turns the word over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: the Brontes' Yorkshire is moorland, so moors is an example of Bronte country

explanation.surface: A writer at work on a fresh novel inspired by the rolling Yorkshire landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling' turns MOORS into SROOM, and 'underpins' places NEW under it, making NEW above SROOM in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsroom is the office where journalists write up news reports.

clue.text: Escapade written up in pencil or felt-tip

indicators.note: written up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Recording an adventure using either a pencil or a felt pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters inside 'pencil or felt-tip', and 'written up' reads them upward in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A frolic is a playful escapade or lark, a spell of light-hearted fun.

clue.text: After record's brought up, office workers fish for pay-off

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a record such as a ship's log; the 's is just a link
a den is a private study or office
hands are manual workers
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: After a record is raised at a meeting, staff angle for a severance payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses the record upward in this down light; 'office workers' looks like one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A generous lump sum paid to a departing executive is a pay-off of this kind.

clue.text: Rearing animal beginning to pounce on insect

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the earlier pieces above the insect

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, an animal

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of the word pounce

parts.note: an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A beast rearing up, about to spring on a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry a lion rampant stands on its hind legs, which is why 'Rearing' fits.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a rampant beast is shown upright on its hind legs, the posture of rearing.

clue.text: Elastic band through nose

indicators.note: through puts the band piece running inside the other word

parts.note: to nose about is to spy
a ring is a band, as a wedding band

explanation.surface: An elastic band threaded through the nose, like a piercing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nose' is a verb here: to nose around is to snoop, or spy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something springy bounces back into shape, which is what an elastic material does.

clue.text: Rough crowd hoot at member of Lords on TV

indicators.note: rough suggests a rough handling, roughing up the letters of the two words into a new order

explanation.surface: A rowdy audience jeering at a peer appearing on television.
explanation.walkthrough: The Doctor is a Time Lord in the BBC science-fiction series, so 'Lords' are not the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of the long-running BBC show is a Time Lord from Gallifrey.

clue.text: Primate catching bird with both hands

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so the bird is held between the letters

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right, the two hands
the emu is a large flightless bird

explanation.surface: A primate grabbing a bird with both its hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are primates found in Madagascar, related to monkeys and apes.

clue.text: I fought with climber all over the place

definitions.text: with climber all over the place

parts.note: vied means competed or fought

explanation.surface: Someone describing a scrap with a mountaineer that went everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' is not a mountaineer but a climbing plant, ivy, and 'all over the place' is part of the definition, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivied walls are covered with ivy, the climbing plant spread across them.

clue.text: Cause a fuss like the First Lady did?

definitions.text: Cause a fuss like the First Lady did?

parts.words: Cause a fuss like the First Lady did?
parts.note: the idiom for creating an uproar, read literally: Eve, the first woman, brought up her son, Abel's killer

explanation.surface: Kicking up a row in the manner of a president's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's wife, but here it is Eve, who raised her son Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make a loud commotion or protest; Eve literally reared Cain.

clue.text: Performance a failure — a measure of speed required

parts.note: a gig is a live performance
a flop is a failure

explanation.surface: A show that bombed, with a speed reading demanded afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigaflop is a billion floating-point operations per second, a unit of computer speed.

clue.text: Church legal representative specialising in verbal exchanges

parts.note: atty is the abbreviation for attorney

explanation.surface: A church lawyer whose speciality is spoken argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatty person loves talking and conversation, so is given to verbal exchanges.

clue.text: Excited fan of tube leaving terminus — like High Barnet?

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so these letters are rearranged
leaving terminus means the word tube drops its end letter

explanation.surface: A thrilled Underground enthusiast reaching High Barnet, at the end of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: High Barnet is a Northern line terminus, but 'barnet' is British rhyming slang (Barnet Fair) for hair. 'leaving terminus' drops the final E, then 'Excited' mixes FAN OF TUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A barnet piled high is hair puffed up and backcombed, the bouffant style.

clue.text: Note one function turning into another

definitions.note: short for another function, a different sense of the word: a party or gathering

indicators.note: turning means the whole sequence of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: la is a note in the sol-fa scale
I is the Roman numeral for one
cos, cosine, is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A musical note and a maths function morphing into something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses LA + I + COS; the result is 'another' function, a gathering rather than a mathematical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is a party or get-together, which is a function in the event sense.

clue.text: Ability to keep going makes lively mounts expend energy

indicators.note: expend means use up, so the energy letter is spent and goes
mounts means climbs, so in a down light the word is read upwards

parts.note: to animate is to make lively
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Spirited horses that use up energy need endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounts' looks like horses, but it is a verb: ANIMATES climbs to SETAMINA, then 'expend' drops an E.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the endurance to continue for a long time.

clue.text: Conservative with iffy seat (majority vulnerable ultimately) which reflects middle-of-the-road views

indicators.note: iffy means dodgy, so these letters are jumbled
ultimately takes the last letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A Tory MP in a marginal seat, his majority shaky, who is a centrist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle-of-the-road' sounds political but is literal: these studs mark the centre of the road. 'iffy' makes ATSE from SEAT; YE comes from majority and vulnerable.
explanation.definitionFit: These reflective road studs show drivers the centre line in the dark.

clue.text: Rent troubles — one such prompted Dorothy's relocation

definitions.note: one such refers to one of the plural answer's kind, the twister that carried Dorothy to Oz

parts.note: rent as a past tense means torn
ados are troubles or fusses

explanation.surface: Rent arrears and disputes forced a tenant called Dorothy to move house.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Wizard of Oz a twister lifts Dorothy's Kansas house and drops it in Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlwind of this kind swept Dorothy from Kansas to the land of Oz.

clue.text: Visual arts show said by some to have terrible security protection

indicators.note: said by some means in some accents, without a sounded R, these words sound like the entry

parts.note: terrible means dire; protective covering for security is armour

explanation.surface: A visual arts show criticised for its awful security arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' are speakers of non-rhotic English, who drop the R sounds in DIRE ARMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional scene model displayed in museums, a kind of visual exhibit.

clue.text: Formal chief in filthy surroundings

indicators.note: in places the chief word inside the filthy place

parts.note: a sty, pigsty, is notoriously filthy surroundings
arch means chief, as in archenemy

explanation.surface: A buttoned-up boss living in squalor.
explanation.definitionFit: Starchy describes someone stiff and prim in manner, as if starched, which is formal.

clue.text: Pope's man, member of holy order with chinos, oddly

parts.note: a nun belongs to a religious order

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of chinos

explanation.surface: A papal envoy who is a nun wearing casual trousers, oddly enough.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuncio is the Vatican's ambassador, the Pope's representative in a country.

clue.text: Run in first of Arab white horses on special surface

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of Arab
in puts the run piece inside the sea foam word

parts.note: white horses are foam-crested waves, or surf
to trot is to run at a gentle pace

explanation.surface: An Arab horse cantering among white horses on an artificial track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white horses' are not animals but the foaming crests of waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Astroturf is the brand of artificial grass used on sports pitches, a special playing surface.

clue.text: Motor trouble returns after second kilometre

indicators.note: after places the reversed trouble word behind the two abbreviations

parts.note: K is short for kilometre

indicators.note: returns means the trouble word is read backwards

parts.note: ado means trouble or fuss

explanation.surface: Car trouble comes back just one second and a kilometre into the drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Skoda is a Czech car maker, so one of its cars is a motor.

clue.text: I'm selling a dream

parts.note: I'm gives the pronoun I, with am going into the verb that follows
I deal means I am selling, as a trader deals in goods

explanation.surface: A salesperson pitching a fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I'm selling' as 'I deal'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect vision or aspiration, the stuff of dreams.

clue.text: Daily punishment perhaps accepted by Milan team coach

parts.note: a daily is a British cleaning lady, also called a char

indicators.note: accepted by means held inside, so the punishment goes within the team letters

parts.note: AC Milan is the Italian football club
a ban is one kind of punishment

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports a club's coach being suspended as punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' in Britain is a cleaner, a char, not a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an old-fashioned motor coach used for outings.

clue.text: Shocking treatment of heavy prisoner at Strangeways?

indicators.note: Strangeways, a Manchester prison, is read as strange ways, so these letters are arranged in an odd way

explanation.surface: Electroshock punishment handed out to a tough inmate in a Manchester jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Strangeways is a well-known Manchester prison, so the surface paints a jail scene; read as 'strange ways' it tells you to rearrange the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: This behavioural conditioning uses discomfort, often electric shocks, to make patients dislike a habit.
